name: Four on the Floor
description: Kick on every quarter note — the backbone of disco, house, and rock.

name: Backbeat
description: Snare on beats 2 and 4 — the defining feel of rock and pop.

name: Standard Rock Beat
description: Kick on quarters with hi-hat 8ths — the most common rock drum pattern.

name: Half-time Feel
description: Snare on beat 3 only — creates a slow, heavy groove.

name: Double-time Feel
description: Driving 8th-note pulse that doubles the perceived tempo.

name: Bo Diddley Beat
description: A hambone-derived pattern that became a rock-and-roll staple.

name: Tresillo
description: The 3-side of clave — a foundational Afro-Latin cell heard worldwide.

name: Son Clave 3-2
description: The classic Cuban clave that underpins salsa, son, and timba.

name: Son Clave 2-3
description: Son clave reversed — the 2-side leads.

name: Rumba Clave 3-2
description: A shifted third stroke gives rumba its distinctive push.

name: Rumba Clave 2-3
description: Rumba clave with the 2-side leading.

name: Bossa Nova Clave
description: Son clave with an added note — the rhythmic DNA of bossa nova.

name: Cáscara (shell pattern)
description: Played on the timbale shell — interlocks with clave in salsa.

name: Montuno (basic)
description: The piano guajeo skeleton that drives salsa and son montuno.

name: Tumbao (basic conga)
description: The fundamental conga pattern — open tones on the and-of-4 and the and-of-2.

name: Mozambique
description: A Cuban carnival rhythm created by Pello el Afrokán.

name: Songo
description: A modern Cuban groove blending rumba and funk — popularised by Los Van Van.

name: Nanigo / Abakuá
description: A sacred Abakuá rhythm that influenced rumba and jazz.

name: Samba Surdo (first)
description: The deep surdo marks beats 1 and 3 — the heartbeat of samba.

name: Samba Surdo (second / response)
description: The answering surdo on beats 2 and 4.

name: Partido Alto
description: A syncopated samba sub-genre pattern central to pagode and MPB.

name: Samba Telecoteco
description: The agogô/tamborim timeline that gives samba its swing.

name: Baião
description: The zabumba pattern of forró and baião from northeast Brazil.

name: Maracatu
description: An Afro-Brazilian carnival rhythm from Recife.

name: Ijexá
description: A Candomblé-derived rhythm central to Bahian carnival and axé music.

name: Standard Pattern (West African bell)
description: The asymmetric 12-pulse timeline mapped to 16 steps — the most widespread African bell pattern.

name: Bembé / 12-8 bell
description: A 7-stroke bell cycle common in 12/8 West African and Afro-Cuban music.

name: Kpanlogo
description: A Ga recreational dance rhythm from Accra.

name: Gahu
description: An Ewe social-dance bell pattern.

name: Fume-Fume
description: An Ewe processional rhythm.

name: Highlife Timeline
description: The guitar/bell timeline of classic highlife.

name: Afrobeat (Tony Allen snare)
description: Tony Allen's displaced snare pattern — the engine of Fela Kuti's Afrobeat.

name: Soukous / Cavacha
description: The snare/guitar timeline of Congolese soukous and cavacha dance.

name: One Drop
description: Kick and snare together on beat 4 only — the signature of roots reggae.

name: Steppers / Four on the Floor Reggae
description: Kick on every quarter — a driving reggae variant.

name: Rockers Reggae
description: Kick on 1, snare on 4 — Sly Dunbar's modernisation of one-drop.

name: Ska Offbeat
description: Guitar/keys chop on every offbeat 8th — the original ska skank.

name: Dancehall (Sleng Teng era)
description: A digital-era dancehall pattern with syncopated kick.

name: Calypso
description: The iron/conga pattern of Trinidad calypso and soca.

name: Soca (modern power soca)
description: A driving carnival groove — bass drum on quarters with syncopated accents.

name: Funk (James Brown / Clyde Stubblefield)
description: The 'Funky Drummer' skeleton — arguably the most sampled groove in history.

name: Funk Backbeat 16ths
description: A busy 16th-note funk groove with ghost notes on the e's and a's.

name: New Orleans Second Line
description: The snare-driven parade beat of New Orleans brass bands.

name: Go-Go (DC)
description: The conga-driven groove of DC go-go — a perpetual-motion funk machine.

name: Motown (Four on the Floor + tambourine 8ths)
description: Benny Benjamin's driving Motown pulse — kick quarters plus tambourine 8ths.

name: Purdie Shuffle
description: Bernard Purdie's half-swung shuffle with ghost notes — a studio legend.

name: Hip-Hop Boom-Bap
description: The classic East-Coast hip-hop kick-snare pattern.

name: Swing Ride Pattern (straight-grid approximation)
description: The jazz ride cymbal pattern approximated on a straight 16th grid.

name: Bebop Comping (Charleston base)
description: The Charleston rhythm used as a comping skeleton in bebop.

name: Jazz Waltz Ride (mapped to 4/4)
description: A 3/4 ride pattern proportionally mapped into a 16-step bar.

name: Boogaloo (Latin Jazz)
description: A 1960s Latin-soul hybrid groove.

name: House Four-on-the-Floor + Open Hat
description: Kick on quarters, open hi-hat on 8th offbeats — classic house.

name: Garage / 2-Step
description: A skippy, syncopated kick pattern that defines UK garage.

name: Drum & Bass (Amen break skeleton)
description: The Amen break's accent skeleton — the backbone of jungle and DnB.

name: Breakbeat (Think break)
description: Lyn Collins 'Think' break — a staple of breakbeat and big beat.

name: Trap (basic hi-hat)
description: Rapid hi-hat 8ths (often 16ths/32nds) over a sparse kick-snare.

name: Trap (kick-snare skeleton)
description: The sparse, booming kick-snare of modern trap.

name: Dembow (Reggaetón)
description: The Dem Bow riddim — the universal engine of reggaetón.

name: Moombahton
description: A half-tempo dembow variant blending reggaetón with Dutch house.

name: Techno (basic)
description: Minimal four-on-the-floor with emphasis on timbre over rhythm.

name: Cumbia (basic)
description: The güira/tambora pattern of Colombian cumbia.

name: Cumbia Sonidera / Rebajada
description: A slowed, bass-heavy Mexican reinterpretation of cumbia.

name: Merengue
description: Driving 8th-note güira with tambora accents — the national rhythm of the DR.

name: Bachata
description: A syncopated guitar-driven pattern with a signature bass anticipation.

name: Bolero (Afro-Cuban / pan-Latin)
description: A slow, romantic rhythm shared across Cuba, Mexico, and the Americas.

name: Reggaetón Dembow (full two-bar)
description: The full two-bar dembow cycle with kick and snare placement.

name: Maqsoum
description: The most common Arabic rhythm — D-k---D-kD------.

name: Baladi
description: A heavier, earthier cousin of maqsoum — the 'of the country' rhythm.

name: Saidi
description: An Upper-Egyptian folk rhythm — similar to maqsoum but with a heavier feel.

name: Ayub / Zaar
description: A driving two-beat trance/ritual rhythm — D-k-----D-------.

name: Malfuf
description: A fast 2/4 rhythm common in Egyptian pop and belly-dance finales.

name: Ciftetelli / Wahda Kebira
description: A slow, ornamental rhythm used in belly-dance taxim sections.

name: Karachi / Khaliji
description: A Gulf-region rhythm popular in khaliji pop and dance.

name: Samai Thaqil 10/8 (mapped)
origin: Middle Eastern / North African (Ottoman / Arab art music)
description: A 10-beat Ottoman/Arab art-music cycle proportionally mapped to 16 steps.

name: Jurjina 10/16
description: A 10-pulse Iraqi/Turkish cycle with a distinctive lopsided lilt.

name: Tintal 16-beat (accent cycle)
description: The four vibhag accents of the 16-matra Tintal — the most common Hindustani tala.

name: Jhaptal 10-beat (mapped)
description: A 10-beat tala (2+3+2+3) proportionally mapped to 16 steps.

name: Rupak 7-beat (mapped)
description: A 7-beat tala (3+2+2) mapped to 16 steps — starts on a khali (wave).

name: Dadra 6-beat (mapped)
description: A 6-beat cycle (3+3) used in thumri and ghazal, mapped to 16 steps.

name: Adi Tala / Chatusra-jati Triputa (accent cycle)
description: The 8-beat Carnatic tala with laghu + two drutam clap accents.

name: Misra Chapu (accent cycle)
description: A 7-akshara chapu feel reduced to its larger grouping accent points.

name: Khanda Chapu (accent cycle)
description: A 5-akshara asymmetrical cycle compressed into one 16-step bar.

name: Keherwa / Kaharwa (accent cycle)
description: An 8-beat cycle reduced to its two big halves for easy groove mapping.

name: Rachenitsa / Ruchenitsa 7/8
description: A 2+2+3 additive dance meter proportionally fit to 16 steps.

name: Lesnoto 7/8
description: A 3+2+2 additive dance meter common across Balkan folk traditions.

name: Karsilama 9/8
description: A face-to-face dance rhythm usually grouped in a 2+2+2+3 contour.

name: Kopanitsa 11/8
description: A lively Bulgarian 11-beat dance with a strongly asymmetrical additive pulse.

name: Take Five 5/4
description: The familiar 3+2 five-beat grouping associated with 'Take Five' and related 5/4 grooves.
